summary_paragraph: The patient, a morbidly obese male with HLA-B27 positive ankylosing spondylitis, hypertension, asthma, obstructive sleep apnea, and anxiety, was admitted for acute-on-chronic bilateral sacroiliac and hip joint pain. He had recently increased his prednisone to 40 mg without relief and missed a planned methylprednisolone infusion. Admission labs showed mild inflammation with normal blood cultures and a contaminated urine culture. Imaging confirmed stable sacroiliitis without infection. He received CT-guided bilateral sacroiliac joint steroid injections, after which his pain improved and he was weaned from IV to oral pain medication. His lisinopril was increased for hypertension, and asthma and anxiety were managed with home medications. The rheumatology plan includes starting a TNF-alpha inhibitor (Symponi) with infectious disease screening completed, including a negative Quantiferon test. He will taper prednisone after initiating biologic therapy and begin Bactrim prophylaxis. He was discharged home with follow-up arranged in rheumatology, pain management, and primary care.
problems: Ankylosing spondylitis sacral and sacrococcygeal region
Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
